title: Boundary lifting for local equivalences of hypercover-local simplicial presheaves
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with a Grothendieck topology $J$ given by covering sieves: a sieve is a set of arrows into an object closed under precomposition, the maximal sieve covers, and covering sieves satisfy pullback stability and transitivity. No fibre products or subcanonicity are assumed. Use [def-weil-size-convention] for universes and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] for associated sheaves.

Write $h_T(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,T)$. A hypercover $U_\bullet\to h_T$ is an augmented simplicial presheaf of sets whose terms are small coproducts of representables and whose augmented matching maps become epimorphisms after sheafification. The degree-zero matching presheaf is $h_T$; all higher matching presheaves, parametrizing compatible proper faces, are formed in presheaves. A refinement over $T$ means a morphism of augmented simplicial presheaves over $h_T$. A collection is dense if every hypercover over every $T$ admits a refinement by a member of that collection over the same $T$.

Let $H$ be a small dense set of these hypercovers. Give $\mathsf U(\mathcal C)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{sSet})$ the projective model structure with objectwise weak homotopy equivalences and Kan fibrations, and its left Bousfield localization $\mathsf U(\mathcal C)_H$ at the augmentation maps $U_\bullet\to h_T$ in $H$ [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-localization-comparison]. In this localization cofibrations are the projective cofibrations, fibrant objects are the projectively fibrant $H$-local objects, and $H$-local means that every augmentation in $H$ induces an equivalence of projectively derived mapping spaces into that object. Use simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. A Kan complex is a simplicial set with fillers for all horns. The standard simplex $\Delta^n$ is the simplicial set represented by $[n]$, its boundary $\partial\Delta^n$ is the union of its proper faces, and a horn is the union of all faces except one. For objectwise Kan simplicial presheaves, a local weak equivalence means an isomorphism on the associated sheaves of $\pi_0$ and, for every $V\in\mathcal C$, vertex $x\in X(V)_0$ and $m\ge1$, an isomorphism on the associated sheaves on $\mathcal C/V$ of the homotopy groups $\pi_m(X|_{\mathcal C/V},x)\to\pi_m(Y|_{\mathcal C/V},f(x))$. Here $\mathcal C/V$ has the induced covering-sieve topology.

If $p:X\to Y$ is a fibration in $\mathsf U(\mathcal C)_H$, both $X$ and $Y$ are fibrant there, and $p$ is a local weak equivalence, then $p$ is an objectwise trivial Kan fibration. More explicitly, for every $T\in\mathcal C$ and $n\ge0$, every commutative square with left map $h_T\times\partial\Delta^n\to h_T\times\Delta^n$ and right map $p$ has a diagonal lift.
